# dsh-secret-form
A **one-time web link for secrets** in DeepSeek Harness.

The model needs an API key. Today the usual answer is "paste it in the chat",
which puts the secret

into the session log, the transcript, every later provider
request, and anything the session is expo

rted to. This plugin replaces that with
a link:

1. the model calls `secret_create` and gets an absolute URL;
2. the human opens it on a phone or a d

esktop, types the value, presses Save;
3. the plugin writes it into the host credential store or int

The page is one self-contained HTML document: inline CSS, no assets, no
frameworks, light and dark f
rom the same markup.
## Install

The package ships a `dsh.bundle` layer, so `dsh plugin add` both installs it and
mounts it: it shows

up in the settings plugin list, where it can be switched off
or removed like any other plugin. Host

-specific settings belong in the profile's
own patch as an id-targeted override.
### From npm

### From GitHub

Pin a tag when you want a revision you can point at later; the repository root is
the package, so no
build step is involved.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Either way the package ships no `dsh.bundle`, so it lands as a plain dependency
and the profile patc
h row below is what actually mounts it.

Mount it next to the two services it uses — the Web GUI host and the agent's
tools:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`publicUrl` matters behind a proxy: the listener usually binds loopback, so its
own origin would pro

duce a `http://127.0.0.1:3080/...` link that no phone can
open. When `publicUrl` is set the returned

link is built from it; when it is not,
the plugin returns the listener origin unchanged and the mod

el is told to hand it
over as-is rather than invent a hostname.

`routePrefix` moves the whole surface, which is what a host behind a path
rewriter needs. `defaultTt

lSeconds` is the TTL used when a call omits
`ttlSeconds`. `defaultLocale` is the wording used when n

either the link nor the
browser asks for a language; any other value is refused at mount time.

The plugin declares `inject: ['tools', 'webServer']`: it cannot do anything
without a Web GUI server

to serve the page, and it registers its four tools on
the agent surface. The credentials service is

read lazily, so a host that only
writes to files does not need a credential provider.
## The four tools
### `secret_create`
Open a form and return its link.
| argument | type | required | meaning |
| `ref` | string | yes | Key name. Default target: the credential reference, such as `OPENAI_API_KEY
`. File target: the path inside the document — `provider.apiKey` for yaml/json, a bare key for `.env

`. |
| `label` | string | yes | Form title, 2 to 5 words. |
| `kind` | `'single'` \| `'multi'` | yes

| One-line masked input, or a monospace textarea for multi-line secrets. |
| `description` | string

| no | One or two sentences under the title, at most 300 characters. |
| `save` | object | no | Def

ault `{ "kind": "credentials" }`. A file target is `{ "kind": "file", "path": "…" }`. |
| `ttlSecond

s` | integer | no | Default 300, clamped to 30..3600. |
| `allowEmpty` | boolean | no | Default `fal

se`. When true an empty submit is accepted and reported as `empty`. |
| `expect` | string | no | Reg
ular expression as text. The result carries `matchesExpect`; the page warns on a mismatch but still

saves. |
| `data` | object | no | Up to 1 KB of bookkeeping for the model. Echoed verbatim by all fo
ur tools, never rendered on the page. |

Returns `{ uuid, url, expiresAt, data }`. `url` is absolute: the web server's
`getOrigin()` plus `ro
utePrefix` plus a 43-character token.
### `secret_result`
| argument | type | required | meaning |

| `uuid` | string | yes | The uuid `secret_create` returned. |
| `waitSeconds` | integer | no | 0..3
0, default 0. Above zero it waits for the form to leave `pending`, then reports whatever state it re
lt 0. Above zero it waits for the form to leave `pending`, then reports whatever state it reached. |

Returns `{ status, data, ref, label }` plus, once a value was submitted,
`length` (characters), `lin

es`, `trimmed` (whether surrounding whitespace was
stripped) and `matchesExpect` when `expect` was g

iven. `status` is one of
`pending`, `saved`, `empty`, `cancelled`, `expired`.

The submitted value never appears in a tool result. Not truncated, not masked,
not hashed — absent.
## Security notes

- **The token is the capability.** 256 bits of `crypto.randomBytes`, base64url,
single use. A succes

sful submit or a cancel kills it: the link still opens, but
only to say "already used" or "cancelled

". Nothing else can read a form.
- **The value only ever travels browser → host.** It is not logged,

not echoed
back into the page, and not returned to the model. Logs carry at most the first
eight ch

aracters of a token.
- **The page never accepts a value twice.** A second POST on the same token is

a
`410` and writes nothing.
- **The page holds no third-party content.** `default-src 'none'` with i

nline
style and script only, `form-action 'self'`, `base-uri 'none'`, no referrer,
no store, no fram

ing.
- **One-time links are visible to whoever can read the chat.** The URL is safe to
post because

it carries no secret; anything that can submit it first wins.
Treat the window as `ttlSeconds`, and

cancel a form you no longer need.
- **A link is bound to this process.** Nothing about it is durable

, which is why
a restart is safe — and why every form disappears with it.
## Why the single-line field is a textarea

Firefox offers its password manager on `input[type=password]`, and on text inputs
it heuristically r

eads as login fields (the same problem the Telegram bot card
hit with its group reference). A `texta

rea` is never treated as a login field, so
the single-line form uses a one-row textarea; the value i

s hidden by an overlay
of bullets rather than by the element type, which keeps the reveal toggle wor

king
in every browser, including those without `-webkit-text-security`.
